paper: General Ability Test, Series A (English items 6-31 that need no passage, and Part B General Knowledge)

questions.q:
Convert from direct into indirect speech.
Ayushi said to the group, "We have had enough of suffering today. It is time to march forward."
o: Ayushi told the group that they had had enough of suffering that day and it was time to march forward
Ayushi asked the group that they had had enough of suffering this day and it was time to march forward
Ayushi told the group that they had enough of suffering and that it is time to march forward
Ayushi told the group that we had had enough of suffering this day and it was time to march forward
questions.e: In reported speech 'we' becomes 'they', 'have had' becomes 'had had', 'today' becomes 'that day' and 'is' becomes 'was'.

questions.q:
Convert from direct speech into indirect speech.
"Where were you last week?" Alok asked Sheela.
o: Alok told Sheela where she had been the week before
Alok asked Sheela where she had been the week before
Alok asked Sheela where she was the week before
Alok asked Sheela where she had been the last week
questions.e: A question is reported with 'asked', past simple 'were' shifts to past perfect 'had been', and 'last week' becomes 'the week before'.

questions.q:
Convert the following sentence from active voice into passive voice.
The king who the people loved built the castle five centuries ago.
o: The castle was built five centuries ago by the king who was loved by the people
The castle was built five centuries ago by the king who loved the people
The castle built five centuries ago by the king loved by the people
The castle was built five centuries ago by the people who were loved by the king
questions.e: The object 'the castle' becomes the subject, and the relative clause also turns passive: 'who was loved by the people'.

questions.q: Select the option that most appropriately describes the meanings of the given pair of words: Seldom and Often
o: Seldom means hardly ever and often means time and again
Seldom means time and again and often means hardly ever
Seldom means never and often means not at all
Seldom means frequently and often means time and again
questions.e: Seldom means hardly ever; often means time and again (frequently).

questions.q: Select the option that most appropriately describes the meanings of the given pair of words: Overcome and Succeed
o: Overcome means triumph over and succeed means to achieve something
Overcome means achieve something and succeed means to triumph over
Overcome means to be successful and succeed means to achieve something
Overcome means winning and succeed means to rise above
questions.e: To overcome is to triumph over a difficulty; to succeed is to achieve something.

questions.q: Select the option that most appropriately describes the meanings of the given pair of words: Emancipate and Empower
o: Emancipate means authorize and empower means liberate
Emancipate means liberate and empower means authorise
Emancipate means liberal and empower means authorisation
Emancipate means freedom and empower means encounter
questions.e: Emancipate means to set free (liberate); empower means to give authority or power.

questions.q:
Select the word nearest in meaning to 'dodgy' as used in the sentence:
The dodgy behaviour of the leader led to her fall.
questions.e: 'Dodgy' means dishonest or unreliable.

questions.q:
Select the word nearest in meaning to 'inclement' as used in the sentence:
People have been advised not to venture into sea as the weather is likely to be inclement.
questions.e: 'Inclement' weather is rough and stormy, closest to 'squally'.

questions.q:
Directions: The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences of a passage are given. Arrange the middle sentences P, Q, R and S in the proper order.
S1. Sufism is an English word coined in the Nineteenth Century.
P. Historians have understood this term in several ways.
Q. According to some scholars, it is derived from suf, meaning wool.
R. Others derive it from safa, meaning purity.
S. The word used for Sufism in Islamic texts is tasawwuf.
S6. It may also have been suffa, the platform outside a place of Islamic worship.
questions.e: S gives the Islamic term, P says historians read it in many ways, Q and R give the suf and safa origins, and S6 adds suffa.

questions.q:
Directions: The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences of a passage are given. Arrange the middle sentences P, Q, R and S in the proper order.
S1. Al-Biruni was born in 973, in Khwarizm in present-day Uzbekistan.
P. In 1017, when Sultan Mahmud invaded Khwarizm, he took several scholars back to his capital, Ghazni: Al-Biruni was one among them.
Q. He was well versed in several languages: Syriac, Arabic, Persian, Hebrew and Sanskrit.
R. Khwarizm was an important centre of learning, and Al-Biruni received the best education available at the time.
S. However he did not know Greek, although he was familiar with the works of Plato and other Greek philosophers.
S6. He arrived in Ghazni as a hostage, but gradually developed a liking for the city.
questions.e: R (education in Khwarizm) leads to Q (languages), S (but no Greek), then P (taken to Ghazni in 1017), which links to S6.

questions.q:
Directions: The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences of a passage are given. Arrange the middle sentences P, Q, R and S in the proper order.
S1. Vijayanagara or 'city of victory' was the name of both a city and an empire.
P. In its heyday it stretched from the river Krishna in the north to the extreme south of the Indian peninsula.
Q. Although it fell into ruin in the seventeenth-eighteenth centuries, it continued to live in the memories of the people who inhabited the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab.
R. In 1565 the city was sacked and subsequently deserted.
S. The Empire was founded in the fourteenth century.
S6. They remembered it as Hampi, a name derived from that of the local mother goddess, Pampadevi.
questions.e: Founded in the 14th century (S), its extent (P), sacked in 1565 (R), and remembered in memory (Q) leads to S6 about Hampi.

questions.q:
Directions: The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences of a passage are given. Arrange the middle sentences P, Q, R and S in the proper order.
S1. Liberalisation and globalisation freed India's economy from the low GDP trap that had impeded India's progress.
P. India's 3 per cent rate of growth and a set of emergent circumstances led to a balance of payment crisis in the early 1990s.
Q. Ease of business was ensured, and the requirement for import licences and production quotas were removed.
R. Apart from these measures India also took a loan from the IMF to tide over the crisis, but after 1993, India has not taken another loan from the IMF.
S. In a landmark budget in 1991, responding to the emergent crisis, India delicenced many industries and liberalised its economic policies.
S6. Today India has transformed into one of the largest economies of the world.
questions.e: Low growth caused the crisis (P), the 1991 budget responded (S), ease of business followed (Q), and the IMF loan (R) completes it.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word or phrase:
I can't be bothered to tell him what I think; ________ he would not listen to me.
questions.e: 'In any case' means whatever happens, fitting 'he would not listen anyway'.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word or phrase:
________, have you been to the local library yet?
questions.e: 'Incidentally' introduces a new, by-the-way question.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word or phrase:
________, women are healthier and are living longer than ever before: indeed on an average, they can expect to live five years longer than men.
questions.e: 'To a large extent' fits a broad general claim about women's health and lifespan.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word or phrase:
The difference is that I have been fortunate to find a career that I love and, ________, I am getting paid reasonably for it.
questions.e: 'What is more' adds an extra positive point.

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word or phrase:
________, the Government of India has followed the policy of trying to improve relations with its neighbours.
questions.e: 'In general' introduces an overall policy trend.

questions.q: The focal length of a concave lens is 0.5 m. The power of the lens is
questions.e: Power P = 1/f; for a concave lens f = -0.5 m, so P = -2.0 D.

questions.q: The rule to determine the direction of a force experienced by a straight current carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field which is perpendicular to it is
questions.e: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements for second law of motion is NOT correct?
o: The net force on a body is proportional to that body's acceleration
The net force on a body is in the same direction as the acceleration
The time rate of change of momentum is equal to force
The net force on a body is proportional to that body's momentum
questions.e: Newton's second law says net force is proportional to acceleration (rate of change of momentum), not to momentum itself.

questions.q: The temperature of a body increases from 310 K to 340 K. The temperature increase in degree Celsius is
questions.e: A rise of 30 K is the same as a rise of 30 °C, since both scales have equal-sized degrees.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements for the work done by gravity on a body is NOT correct?
o: Work done is independent of the path followed by the body
Work done depends only on the vertical distance separating the initial and the final position of the body
Work done depends on the path followed by the body
Work done is zero if the body is displaced horizontally to the force of gravity
questions.e: Gravity is a conservative force, so its work depends only on the start and end heights, not on the path.

questions.q: Which one among the following statements is correct?
o: Pressure has magnitude as well as direction
As we go deeper in a liquid, the pressure decreases
Action and reaction forces act on the same object
Pascal and N/m² represent the same unit
questions.e: 1 pascal = 1 N/m²; pressure is a scalar, it increases with depth, and action-reaction act on different bodies.

questions.q: In a Telescope, compared to the eyepiece lens the objective lens has
o: larger focal length and larger aperture
larger focal length and smaller aperture
smaller focal length and larger aperture
smaller focal length and smaller aperture
questions.e: A telescope's objective has a large focal length and a large aperture to gather more light.

questions.q: The energy, E, of a photon can be expressed as E = hf where f is the frequency and h is Planck's constant. The dimensions of h are the same as that of
questions.e: h = E/f has units J·s, the same dimensions as angular momentum.

questions.q: The work done by the force acting on an object is zero if the displacement of the object
o: is in the opposite direction of the direction of force
is in the same direction of the direction of force
is in perpendicular direction of the direction of force
questions.e: Work = Fd cos θ, which is zero when the displacement is perpendicular to the force.

questions.q: The magnetic field inside a current carrying very long solenoid is
questions.e: Inside a long solenoid the magnetic field is nearly uniform.

questions.q: Which one of the following instruments can be used to measure -250°C temperature?
o: By using a mercury based thermometer
By using an alcohol based thermometer
questions.e: Mercury and alcohol freeze well above -250 °C, so a thermocouple thermometer is used for such low temperatures.

questions.q: The quantity of heat needed to change unit mass of a substance from liquid to vapour without changing the temperature, is called
questions.e: Heat needed to change unit mass from liquid to vapour at constant temperature is the specific latent heat (of vaporisation).

questions.q: The temperature at which "vapour pressure of the liquid in an open vessel becomes equal to the atmospheric pressure" is called
questions.e: A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the atmospheric pressure.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about surface tension is correct?
o: It will remain same with increase or decrease of temperature
It will always decrease with increase or decrease of temperature
questions.e: Surface tension decreases as temperature increases.

questions.q: A body sinks in water when
o: density of water is greater than density of body
density of water is less than density of body
density of water is equal to density of body
questions.e: A body sinks when its density is greater than that of water.

questions.q: Why a fielder in the ground gradually pulls his hands backward while catching a fast moving cricket ball?
o: To reduce the acceleration of the ball
To increase the acceleration of the ball
To increase the velocity of the ball
questions.e: Pulling the hands back increases the stopping time, which lowers the ball's deceleration and the force on the hands.

questions.q: Bottom of a tank containing water appears to be raised. It is due to
questions.e: Light bends (refracts) when it leaves water, so the bottom looks raised.

questions.q: SONAR stands for
questions.e: SONAR stands for Sound Navigation and Ranging.

questions.q: Which one of the following radiations has longer wavelength?
questions.e: Among these, microwaves have the longest wavelength.

questions.q: A person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly. The person is suffering from
questions.e: Seeing near objects clearly but not distant ones is myopia (short-sightedness).

questions.q: The energy is always conserved for a system which is
questions.e: Total energy is conserved only for an isolated system, which exchanges no energy with its surroundings.

questions.q: Suppose a ball of mass M is thrown upwards from a point A and it reaches up to the highest point B and returns back to point A. Which one among the following is correct?
o: Kinetic Energy at A = Potential Energy at B
Kinetic Energy at A = Potential Energy at A
Kinetic Energy at B = Potential Energy at B
Kinetic Energy at B = Kinetic Energy at A
questions.e: With no air resistance, all kinetic energy at A becomes potential energy at the top point B.

questions.q: Who among the following presided over the first session of All India Kisan Sabha in Lucknow in April 1936?
questions.e: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati presided over the first All India Kisan Sabha session at Lucknow in 1936.

questions.q: Who among the following founded the 'Self-Respect Movement'?
questions.e: E.V. Ramaswami Naicker (Periyar) started the Self-Respect Movement in 1925.

questions.q: Chola inscriptions mention several categories of lands. Which one of the following was meant for the maintenance of school?
questions.e: In Chola inscriptions, shalabhoga was land given to maintain a school.

questions.q: In the Harappan Civilization, traces of canals have been found at
questions.e: Traces of canals of the Harappan period were found at Shortughai in Afghanistan.

questions.q:
Arrange the following foreign travellers to India in chronological order, beginning with the earliest :
1. Peter Mundy
2. Antonio Monserrate
3. Afanasii Nikitich Nikitin
4. Ibn Battuta
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: Ibn Battuta (14th c.), Nikitin (15th c.), Monserrate (16th c.) and Peter Mundy (17th c.) give the order 4-3-2-1.

questions.q: With which of the following was the Bretton Woods System NOT associated
o: Economic recovery after the Second World War
International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
Establishment of a monetary system based on floating exchange rate
questions.e: Bretton Woods set up the IMF and World Bank with fixed exchange rates, not floating rates.

questions.q: The Ramacharita, an example of dvyasrya-kavya, telling two stories simultaneously, was written by
questions.e: Sandhyakara Nandi wrote the Ramacharita, which tells the stories of Rama and the Pala king Ramapala together.

questions.q: Which of the following Acts established the Board of Control to guide and control the work of the Court of Directors and the Government of India?
questions.e: Pitt's India Act, 1784 created the Board of Control over the Company's Court of Directors.

questions.q: Who among the following Sikh Gurus laid the foundation of the Khalsa Panth?
questions.e: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699.

questions.q: Which one among the following plans is also known as Mahalanobis Plan?
questions.e: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61) was based on the Mahalanobis model.

questions.q: Which of the following were the years of Annual Plans?
questions.e: Annual Plans were run from 1966 to 1969 (plan holiday) after the Third Plan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about BRICS Summits :
1. The first BRICS Summit was held in Brazil
2. BRICS Summits were held in New Delhi on three occasions
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The first BRICS summit was in Russia (2009), and New Delhi has not hosted three summits, so both statements are wrong.

questions.q:
Which of the following rights under the Constitution of India is/are Fundamental Right(s)?
1. Right to work
2. Right to privacy
3. Right to free and compulsory education in the age bracket of six to eighteen years
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: Privacy is a Fundamental Right (Puttaswamy, 2017); free education is for ages 6-14, and right to work is a Directive Principle.

questions.q: Which one of the following committees is NOT associated with decentralization of Panchayati Raj institutions in India?
questions.e: Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta and L.M. Singhvi committees dealt with Panchayati Raj; Abhijit Sen committee dealt with food prices.

questions.q: The reaction that occurs on passing carbon dioxide gas through lime water is
questions.e: CO2 turns lime water milky: Ca(OH)2 + CO2 → CaCO3 + H2O.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Water of crystallization is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt
The molecular formula of Plaster of Paris is CaSO4·2H2O
Washing soda is used for removing the permanent hardness of water
The atmosphere of Venus is made up of thick white and yellow clouds of sulphuric acid
questions.e: Plaster of Paris is CaSO4·½H2O; CaSO4·2H2O is gypsum.

questions.q: Which one of the following type of medicines is used for treating indigestion?
questions.e: Antacids neutralise excess stomach acid and treat indigestion.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a chemical change?
questions.e: Melting of ice changes only the state, so it is a physical change.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The interconversion of states of matter is a physical change
During burning of a candle, both chemical and physical changes take place
During a physical change, the chemical composition of molecules changes
Rusting of iron is a chemical change
questions.e: In a physical change the chemical composition of molecules does not change.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a heterogeneous mixture?
o: Mixture of sugar and salt crystals
questions.e: Sulphur dissolves in carbon disulphide to form a uniform (homogeneous) solution.

questions.q:
In the following redox reaction, which compound is acting as a reducing agent?
N2H4 + 2H2O2 → N2 + 4H2O
questions.e: N2H4 loses hydrogen and is oxidised to N2, so it is the reducing agent.

questions.q: Which one of the following is considered to be the purest source of water?
questions.e: Rain water is formed by natural distillation, so it is the purest natural source.

questions.q: Which one of the following salts is responsible for temporary hardness of water?
questions.e: Temporary hardness is caused by bicarbonates of calcium and magnesium.

questions.q: Which one of the following is an endothermic reaction?
questions.e: Thermal decomposition of lead nitrate needs heat, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: Which one of the following is known as 'water gas'?
questions.e: Water gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Diamond is hard due to extended covalent bonding in it
Fullerene is composed of five and six membered rings
Diamond is a good conductor of electricity
Graphite is used as a lubricant
questions.e: Diamond has no free electrons, so it is a poor conductor of electricity.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements with reference to Feldspar mineral :
1. Half of the earth's crust is composed of feldspar
2. It has light cream to salmon pink colour
3. Magnesium is a common element in all types of feldspar
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Feldspar makes up about half of the crust and is light cream to salmon pink; silicon and oxygen, not magnesium, are common to all feldspars.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Oceanic trenches are very significant in the study of plate movements
2. Oceanic trenches are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: Ocean trenches mark subduction zones, so they help study plate movement and have volcanoes and strong earthquakes.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements with reference to shadow zones in an event of an earthquake is/are correct?
1. Zone between 105° and 145° from epicentre was identified as the shadow zone for both P-waves and S-waves
2. The shadow zone of P-waves is much larger than that of the S-waves
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: 105°-145° is the shadow zone for both P and S waves, but the S-wave shadow zone is much larger than the P-wave zone.

questions.q: Which one among the following volcanic island chains is NOT associated with mid-oceanic ridge?
questions.e: The Hawaiian Islands formed over a hotspot, not at a mid-ocean ridge.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements with reference to sea waves :
1. The height of waves is determined by wind speed, wind duration, and fetch
2. The energy of a wave is proportional to the square of its height
3. Waves retain most of their energy as they travel across the deep ocean
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Wave height depends on wind speed, duration and fetch; wave energy varies with height squared; waves lose little energy in deep water.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements with reference to soil forming processes is/are correct?
1. Translocation, enrichment, removal and transformation are different classes of soil forming processes
2. In translocation, fine particles are transported downward by eluviation and accumulate in lower horizons by illuviation
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: Soil processes include translocation, enrichment, removal and transformation; fine particles move down by eluviation and collect below by illuviation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements with reference to structure of the Earth's atmosphere :
1. Thickness of the troposphere is greatest at the equator
2. The air temperature of the tropopause is highest above the poles
3. The temperature in troposphere decreases at the rate of 1°F for every 165 m of height
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The troposphere is thickest at the equator and the tropopause is warmer over the poles; temperature falls about 1 °C (not 1 °F) per 165 m.

questions.q:
Which of the following are the factors that cause variation in the amount of insolation on the Earth?
1. Rotation of the earth on its axis
2. Length of the day
3. Distribution of land and water on the earth
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: Insolation varies with Earth's rotation (tilt) and length of day; land-water distribution affects heating, not incoming insolation.

questions.q:
Consider the following conditions favourable for the formation and intensification of Tropical Storms :
1. Presence of the Coriolis force
2. Upper divergence above the sea level system
3. High variations in the vertical wind speed
Which of the conditions given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Tropical storms need Coriolis force and upper-level divergence; strong vertical wind shear prevents them.

questions.q:
Which of the following factors influence the ocean currents?
1. Coriolis force
2. Gravity
3. Heating by solar energy
4. Wind
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: Ocean currents are driven by solar heating, wind, gravity and the Coriolis force.

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are warm ocean current(s)?
1. Alaska Current
2. Agulhas Current
3. Falkland Current
4. West Australian Current
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: The Alaska and Agulhas currents are warm; the Falkland and West Australian currents are cold.

questions.q: State of Assam shares borders with how many other countries and Indian states respectively?
questions.e: Assam borders Bhutan and Bangladesh and seven states: Arunachal, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya and West Bengal.

questions.q:
Laterite soil in India is rich in which of the following?
1. Calcium
2. Nitrogen
3. Phosphate
4. Potash
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: As per NCERT, laterite soils are rich in iron oxide and potash but poor in nitrogen, phosphate and calcium.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements with reference to crops cultivated in India is/are correct?
1. Bajra grows well in sandy and shallow black soils, whereas red and shallow black soil is suited for Ragi
2. Bajra is predominantly grown in states like Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, while Ragi is mainly cultivated in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Himachal Pradesh
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: Bajra suits sandy and shallow black soils (Rajasthan, UP, Maharashtra) and ragi suits red and shallow black soils (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Himachal).

questions.q: Which one among the following is NOT a beneficiary state from the Vindhyachal Power Plant of the NTPC?
questions.e: Vindhyachal (MP) supplies the western region states like Gujarat, Maharashtra and Goa, not Uttar Pradesh.

questions.q: The book 'The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection' was authored by
questions.e: Charles Darwin wrote 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859.

questions.q: The headquarters of World Meteorological Organization (WMO) is located at
questions.e: The World Meteorological Organization is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.q: The optimum pH at which the enzymes pepsin and trypsin of the human alimentary canal works are
questions.e: Pepsin works best in the acidic stomach (about pH 2) and trypsin in the alkaline intestine (about pH 8).

questions.q: The amount of air breathed in and out during a normal respiration by human lungs is referred to as
questions.e: Air breathed in or out in one normal breath is the tidal volume (about 500 mL).

questions.q: Which one among the following statements about arteries and veins in humans is NOT correct?
o: Arteries carry blood away from heart while veins bring blood towards the heart
Pulmonary arteries always carry oxygenated blood while Pulmonary veins always carry deoxygenated blood
Arteries have thicker and more elastic walls compared to veins in general
Arteries do not have valves but veins do have valves
questions.e: Pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs and pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood back.

questions.q: Identify the functions that are controlled by the hind brain of human being
o: Involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation vomiting etc.
Controlling the regions receiving sensory impulses from receptors
Controlling the movement of voluntary muscles
Sensation of hunger or being full
questions.e: The medulla in the hindbrain controls involuntary actions like blood pressure, salivation and vomiting.

questions.q: Iodized salt is a vital part of our diet as it is essential for the synthesis of
questions.e: Iodine is needed to make the thyroid hormone thyroxine.

questions.q: The menstrual cycle in females is controlled by hormones that are secreted by
questions.e: The menstrual cycle is controlled by pituitary (FSH, LH) and ovarian (estrogen, progesterone) hormones.

questions.q: Which one of the following blood cells type secrete large number of antibodies during an immune response of the body?
questions.e: B-lymphocytes (plasma cells) produce antibodies.

questions.q: Which of the following organelles have their own DNA and ribosomes?
questions.e: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own DNA and ribosomes.

questions.q: What is the nickname of the National Men's Hockey Team of Australia?
questions.e: Australia's men's hockey team is called the Kookaburras.

questions.q: Which one of the following organisations has completed 150 years of service to the nation in the year 2025?
questions.e: The India Meteorological Department, set up in 1875, completed 150 years in 2025.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about 'Jalvahak' is/are correct?
1. It is a newly commissioned naval ship inducted into Indian Navy
2. It is a major policy for cargo promotion unveiled by the Government of India Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: Jalvahak is a cargo promotion scheme for inland waterways launched in 2024, not a naval ship.

questions.q: How many rural districts does Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act cover as on 2024-25?
questions.e: As per the official key, MGNREGA covered about 740 rural districts in 2024-25.

questions.q: Under which one of the following initiatives does the NITI Aayog support interested States to establish a State Institution for Transformation (SIT)?
questions.e: NITI Aayog's State Support Mission helps states set up a State Institution for Transformation.

questions.q: Which one of the following Indian States account for the maximum deposits of Bauxite and Chromite?
questions.e: Odisha has India's largest reserves of both bauxite and chromite.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements with regard to National Technology Day :
1. It commemorates the momentous events of 11th May 1998, when India conducted successful nuclear tests under Operation Shakti
2. The official theme for National Technology Day 2025 is "School | to Startups — Igniting Young Minds to Innovate'
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: National Technology Day (11 May) marks the 1998 Pokhran tests (Operation Shakti); the quoted theme is not the official 2025 theme.

questions.q:
Which of the following were added in India as Ramsar Site in the year 2025?
1. Sakkarakottai Bird Sanctuary
2. Udhwa Lake
3. Rudrasagar Lake
4. Bakhira Wildlife Sanctuary
Select the answer using the code given below :
questions.e: Sakkarakottai Bird Sanctuary (Tamil Nadu) and Udhwa Lake (Jharkhand) were added as Ramsar sites in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Cricket player Virat Kohli :
1. He is the only captain to have scored seven double centuries in Test Cricket
2. He is the only Indian cricketer with most centuries as a captain
3. He is the first Indian captain to achieve twin centuries on captaincy debut
4. He holds the record for the most double centuries by an Indian in Test Cricket
Which of the statements given above are correct?
